scenes.headline: How one runtime serves a model that talks
scenes.sub: Stages, a connector, and an orchestrator that owns the request
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Maestro! A spoken answer from an omni model is three models in a row. Here is how one runtime serves them.

scenes.text: Give every model its own engine and its own batch, and let one orchestrator carry each request from stage to stage.
scenes.say: Every model keeps its own engine and batching, and one orchestrator walks each request through them.

steps.say: A request arrives, and the orchestrator admits it. It owns the request, never the tensors.
The thinker reads the audio and video and writes the text answer.
Each new token sends hidden states to the talker through shared memory.
The talker makes codec frames, the vocoder turns them into sound, and audio streams back.

scenes.title: Two ways to feed the vocoder

left.title: Wait for the reply
items: Vocoder starts when the talker ends
left.say: Without chunking, the vocoder waits for the whole reply.

right.title: Stream chunks
right.say: With chunking, four frames go straight away, then chunks of twenty five, each with earlier frames as context.

scenes.label: first text token at concurrency 32 with chunking switched off
scenes.note: 507.8 ms with chunking on, two H100s
scenes.say: The report's own test: at thirty two concurrent requests, chunking off makes the first token almost seven times later.

scenes.title: Batching a denoiser
scenes.say: Diffusion stages get their own scheduler, because a denoising step is nothing like a decode step.

items.text: Default: one job at a time
items.say: By default, a diffusion stage runs one job from first step to last.
Request mode batches whole jobs, but only jobs with the same size and step count.
Step mode advances every job by one step, so new jobs can join between steps.

scenes.title: Qwen-Image images per second, one H100
scenes.note: Each image now takes 9.66 s instead of 2.42 s
scenes.say: A denoising step is already busy alone. Eight at a time only doubles throughput, and each image takes four times as long.

scenes.text: Unify the request, not the scheduler: decode loops and denoisers keep their own batching under one orchestrator.
scenes.say: So the request is unified, and the schedulers are not.

recap: Stages: one model, one engine each
Chunks stream audio before the reply ends
scenes.say: Stages with their own engines, chunks that stream sound early, and a denoiser that batches its own way.
